meta.title: One fluid size system for the whole site; round 5: fades over whole blocks, hovers that tint and never move, a hero title that fills its cell, blocks that open as one card
meta.lede: The whole system of the QQ Coffee site: 35 size roles drawn as lines from a 320 to a 1440 screen, three shared layout steps and the column at its most, one colour table with one line colour, one motion vocabulary, the 3D packs. Round 5 answers your comments on the home page: four eased fades laid over their whole blocks (and a tuner for them), the place kept when the window resizes, hovers that tint the control's own ground and never move, quiet focus for the pointer, packs without lag, one row of navbar links, a hero title that fills its cell, lines that run to the screen's edges, info blocks that open as one card, and the footer's newsletter in two halves. Measured at every 10px of width and 25px of height and at 25 real screens; «before» is round 4's build (main).
meta.footer: Measured in headless Chromium on the built sites, 2026-10-20. Before = round 4 (main, commit 604abd7); now = branch round-5. Earlier rounds compared with their own previous builds (round 1 with the Figma frames).

blocks.title: What this changes that you may not expect
items: Over the photo the cells are no longer solid black: the photo shows faintly behind the title, the countdown and the links, and on the business cards and the business page's offers the text sits where the fade is 33–38% (the lightest pixels behind an offer title give 2.4:1). The fade tuner can set a curve that darkens sooner, or a reach under 1.
The hero's title is bigger at L (62 → 90px), so at 1440 × 900 the photo above the cells is 20px shorter.

No hover moves anything any more: the photo zooms of the cards, the business cards, the offers and the places, and the sliding arrows of the hero, the business cards, the «Читать» buttons and the row links are gone everywhere, not only where you named them.
Text fields no longer change their border when clicked; the caret is the only sign (the keyboard still gets the ring).
Recommended cards in the margins are gone: at 1920 the right margin no longer shows the next card (a question from round 3).

sections.title: The system
sections.sub: design/scale.json: one range (320 → 1440), one ladder, roles with two ends. build/tokens.mjs writes one clamp() per role and checks the rules.

blocks.title: The ladder
blocks.sub: Steps of 2 up to 24, of 4 up to 64, of 8 up to 128, of 16 up to 256. Every end of every role sits on it (dots).

blocks.title: Text roles
blocks.sub: Value at 320 and 1440 (constant outside), the face, where it is used, and the Figma steps at 320 / 768 / 1280 / 1440 / 1920 where one exists.
rows: section headings, the catalog tabs, the product's name on its page
headings of the image blocks (approach, about)
the name of the featured coffee
names on product cards, titles of tiles (business, info blocks, product facts), footer headings
eyebrows above headings («Наш подход»): set apart by colour and case, not size
the big sentence of a product's story
the caption over the featured photo, the text under a section heading
longer text: the featured description, the story columns, business text
card descriptions, lists, links of the navbar and the footer, fields
descriptor pills, captions above values in the buy bar, the copyright
big actions and values set in bold capitals: hero links, «В корзину», buy-bar values
prices and weights on cards (medium capitals)

blocks.title: Levels that must stay apart
blocks.sub: The ratio of each pair at 320 (light) and at 1440 (dark). Two straight lines keep their ratio between its two end values, so the ends prove every size.

blocks.title: The height counts
blocks.sub: --vp = min(100vw, 2 × 100svh − 25rem): the width a screen counts as. 360 tall → the 320 sizes; 920 tall → the 1440 sizes.
blocks.note: The size a screen gets is the smaller of its width and this line.

Line: how far from the screen's edge the hero's link lines end (0: at the edge; at the frame from 1520). Nav: the hover ground's air beside a link's text. Taste: text to the cell's left / top edge. sections.title: The navbar and the tab bar
sections.sub: Round 2 built it (four steps, the colours of the section under it, one max width with the column, a tab bar on phones); round 5 put the sections in one row, took the profile icon from Figma and evened the hover ground. The table is round 2's measure, round 1 struck.

items.title: Steps
items.html: Every section in one row from 64em (1024, the screen of L); «Каталог, Бизнесу, Журнал, Контакты» from 48em (768, the screen of M); the burger below; under 40em (640) the tab bar. In em, so bigger browser text takes the narrower step sooner. media.css: --links-full, --links, --phone.

items.title: Width
items.html: The bar's margin is 16px (the small gutter); its content min(100% − 2 × (16 − 8), --col-max + 2 × 8): the logo's and icons' boxes carry 8px of air, so the glyphs stand 16px from the edges, and on the column's edges once it is at its most (1616 and up).

items.title: Grounds
items.html: Sections say data-ground (paper, cloud, black, ink); it sets --g-bg, --g-fg, --line and --tint. The bar takes a ground once its whole height is over that section, crossing over in 0.6s; at the top of the page (and above it) the first section's. The tab bar does the same at the foot of the screen.

items.title: Hover
items.html: A tint behind the one item: --tint, white 20% on dark grounds, ink 6% on light ones. 0.2s in, 0.45s out. Nothing else on the bar changes. A link's tint stands 14px from its text on every side (round 5): a ::before 6px wider than the link, which keeps 8px a side, so the texts stay 16px apart and hover areas meet mid-gap.

items.title: Links
items.html: An item links only to a page that exists (data/site.json nav: a second value is the path). Today: «Кофе» and «Каталог». The rest are <a> without href: shown, not clickable, not in the tab order.

items.title: Tab bar
items.html: 56px + the safe area, four equal cells with icon and label (--type-small); the bag's count only. Everything fixed to the foot stands on it through --tabbar-h (the buy bar, the toast, the menu's height, the hero).

blocks.title: The navbar at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Step: what the bar shows. Icons: the tools in the bar. Logo / icon: how far the logo glyph and the last icon glyph stand inside the content column's edges (negative: outside it, in the gutter).

sections.title: The hero
sections.sub: The first screen of the home page. Round 5: the title fills its cell, one fade under the whole block, lines that run out, the whole block rising in. The tables: round 5's measure (round 4 struck), then round 2's.

items.title: Height
items.html: min(100svh − 24 − tab bar, --hero-max), and never less than the navbar + --hero-photo (48 → 120) + --hero-fade (64 → 160) + the cells. --hero-max 960 → 1200 stops a portrait tablet or a 2560 screen (decision hero-height).

items.title: Rows
items.html: Below M the title, the countdown and the links stack. From M the countdown and the links share three equal rows (subgrid), title above; from L the title takes the first cell beside them. Row padding --hero-cell-y 12 → 20; texts trimmed to cap height and baseline.

items.title: Countdown
items.html: Everything as wide as the caption (13.9em of --type-control): the digits are control × 13.9 / 3 in tabular Technology (build/fonts.py), a date control × 13.9 / (0.65 × its letters) in mono. More than 24h to wait shows the date. Moscow time, the placeholder weekday schedule.

items.title: Frame and lines
items.html: Below the column's max the hairlines between cells run out to the screen's edges on the sides where the column ends; at the step max (the column at 1520px) the cells get a hairline on each side, the title 48px of padding, and the lines stop at the frame.

items.title: Fade
items.html: --fade-hero (colors.json fades.hero): 16 stops along a curve («ease» until you tune it), laid under the whole block, cells and all; --hero-fade (64 → 160) of it stands above the hairline (round 5; before: a fade over a black band).

items.title: Title and entrance
items.html: From L the title is a third of the column less its padding, ÷ 4.55 (its longest word), never under --type-display, never over its size at the 1520 column (decision hero-title-fills-cell). The whole block (fade, hairline, cells) rises one section gap and fades in, 0.9s on --ease-out after 0.2s (--t-rise).

blocks.title: The hero at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Before (struck) and now. Peek: what shows of the next block under the hero, above the tab bar (negative: taller than the screen). Lines: the title. Digits / caption: their drawn widths. Align: the largest distance between a link's centre and its countdown part's (from M).

sections.title: New arrivals
sections.sub: One coffee at a time: a text square and a photo square, the pager in the middle of the head. New in round 3.

items.title: Halves
items.html: From L two tracks of minmax(0, 1fr), both aspect-ratio: 1; below L the text above the photo. The text square never grows: scripts/slider.js cuts the story to the whole lines that fit between the name and the taste box (--lines, at most 8).

items.title: Photo
items.html: The coffee's own photo, else the next of featured.photos (four moodboard photos, placeholder); its line over the eased black fade. No hairline beside it.

items.title: Head
items.html: From M three columns 1fr auto 1fr: title, pager, arrows; the pager is in the head's middle wherever the title and arrows are. Below M the pager has its own row.

items.title: Taste box
items.html: The chart's cell has at its sides the air its rows have above them, 12px + (1.75em − 1cap) / 2 (round 5), and stands in its middle when the pills are taller. The taste chart and the pills in two equal halves from M (minmax(min-content, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr): the chart never shrinks, so on 1000–1030 screens its half is up to 12px wider); below M the chart over the pills.

items.title: Link
items.html: The name's link stretched over the slide (::after, z-index 6); the caption above it lets clicks through.

items.title: Swipe and hover
items.html: Still the ordinary scroll-snap row (a magazine-like turn is being chosen in the test bench). The photo no longer zooms on hover; the pager's numbers and the arrows tint their cell (round 5).

blocks.title: New arrivals at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Text / photo: the widths of the two halves (one above the other below L). Heights: text / photo. Taste box: its two cells. Pager: its centre off the head's. Lines: the story's whole lines.

sections.title: The recommended row and the card
sections.sub: The row runs to the screen's edges, but since round 5 its cards show only inside the column: they rise in and sink away. A card is one link; its cells and heart tint on hover.

items.title: Bleed
items.html: The row is widened by the column's margins and padded back (--bleed-l, --bleed-r, measured from the column by script), with scroll-padding the same: its cards stand and snap on the column, but slide out to the screen's edges. Without the script it is the column.

items.title: In the column only
items.html: Out of the column a card waits --section-gap below and clear ([data-wait]). Half in, it rises over --t-rise and fades in over --t-move, the first ones 90ms apart; as soon as it starts crossing out it sinks away over --t-out ([data-wait=out]). On a phone the peeking card counts as in. Not with «reduce motion».

items.title: Packs
items.html: A pack stands exactly in its slot while the page scrolls or the row slides (round 5: no lag, no turn). A card rising into place carries its pack up: it trails and tilts, carryTilt 0.45 at the full trail (12% of its height, ≤ 40px); a card sinking away takes it down upright. A press anywhere on the card moves it away.

items.title: One link
items.html: The name's link is stretched over .card; the picture's layers (photo, pack, name, buy row) share one grid cell, so nothing between is positioned. The heart and the buy row sit above it at z-index 7.

items.title: Hovers
items.html: The weights cell, the price button and the heart tint their ground (--tint: ink 6%, white 20% on a photo card); nothing fades or zooms (round 5). The weights are one cell: a click anywhere picks the other weight.

items.title: Fade
items.html: The buy row is one fade over its whole height (--fade-card-cloud / -black), its 56px lead-in letting clicks through to the card's link.

blocks.sub: Row: its width against the column (it runs to the screen's edges now). First card: its left edge off the column's. Modal: the opened box (width × height; a sheet on a phone).

sections.sub: Three blocks that grow into one modal (Figma info-blocks-modal). Round 5: bigger icons, the plus in the corner, the modal grows as one card.

items.title: Blocks
items.html: Three buttons divided by hairlines (no line above them): the icon (--fact-icon 40 → 56), the title, the ringed plus (32px) 12px in from the corner. Stacked below M, the lines between them run to the screen's edges. Hover: the tint of the ground.

items.title: Modal
items.html: One <dialog> (focus held inside, Esc closes, focus back on its block): a box of --modal-w (360 → 520) over ink 20%; under 40em a sheet at the foot, as wide as the screen. Icon, title (the block's size), the text, the cross; «‹ prev | next ›» step to the other blocks.

items.title: Growing
items.html: One card (round 5): the box starts on the block, cut to its size (clip-path), and grows into place; the icon and title travel at their size, the text rides with the title fading in, the step row slides up from the card's foot, the plus turns 45° into the cross. 0.6s on --ease-out; back the same way. Every box is measured before anything moves.

items.title: Stepping
items.html: Only the text changes: it slides out 24px and fades (0.23s), the next slides in (0.45s). The three panels share one cell, so the box keeps the tallest one's height and the step row (65px at 1440, Figma 66) never moves.

items.title: Live text
items.html: «Ближайшая обжарка через N часов» (or minutes, or the day when it is more than a day away) from the roast schedule, as the hero's countdown.

items.title: Without motion
items.html: With «reduce motion» it simply opens and closes.

sections.title: The footer
sections.sub: Two halves from L, the animated flame, the legal line. New in round 3.

items.title: Squares
items.html: From L two tracks of minmax(0, 1fr); the left half is aspect-ratio: 1 and stretches with the row, so both are square while the links fit (from about 1360 wide), taller where they need more.

items.title: Flame
items.html: Your SMIL file (one path, 109 shapes over 5s, 27 KB gzipped) as a lazy <img>; with «reduce motion» its first frame. --footer-logo wide (104 → 216).

items.title: Optical centre
items.html: The flame's mass centre, measured over its animation (50.5% across, 62.9% down its box), stands on the square's middle: translate(-50.5%, -62.9%). Its box's middle would set it 12% of its height low (the bowl is heavy, the tip thin).

items.title: Legal line
items.html: Copyright and policy: --type-small, ink 70%, one baseline (align-items: baseline), no underline; hover darkens the policy.

items.title: Newsletter
items.html: From M the line and the field are two equal halves (round 5); below M the line over the field.

items.title: Lines and frame
items.html: Below the max the line under each cell runs out to the screen's edge on the sides where the column ends (round 5); at the step max (the column at 1520) a hairline on each side, the texts standing off it by --tile-pad. Links underline on hover in ink 40%, 0.4em below the letters.

blocks.title: The footer at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Brand: the left half (width × height; a square from L where the links fit). Mass: how far the flame's mass centre stands from the square's middle (from L). Legal: the distance between the baselines of the copyright and the policy. News: the newsletter line's lines.

sections.title: The product stage and the buy bar
sections.sub: A coffee's page: the pack pinned while the fact tiles scroll past, the buy bar at the foot.

items.title: Pin
items.html: Height 100svh − navbar − buy bar (at least 22rem), pinned for as long as the five tiles take to pass; the tiles are 40% of the screen's height apart (28% from L), so scroll time is measured in screens (decision product-pin).

items.title: Pack
items.html: --stage 320 → 720, capped by the pin. It turns once around with qqStage.progress; tiles are frosted (cloud 70% + blur 40px) so the pack shows through them.

items.title: Arriving from a card (round 3)
items.html: Opened from a card, the page arrives in a view transition: the card's name becomes the title, its pack the big pack. The pack then starts facing front instead of turning in from a quarter turn.

items.title: Buy bar
items.html: Two rows of cells below L (options; quantity, price, «В корзину»), one row from L as in Figma. On a screen under 32em tall it waits after the stage instead of following the screen, which pins at the whole screen under the navbar (decision short-screens).

blocks.title: The product stage at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Pin: the pinned height. Pack: the 3D box. Under bar: how much of the pack box the buy bar covers. Bar: its height and rows ("after": past the stage on a short screen).

sections.title: The catalog
sections.sub: Tabs, filters kept in the address, the grid.

items.title: Filters
items.html: Seven cells (sort, price of 200 g, type, line, country, processing, preparation) that wrap by width: 7 rows at 320, 4 at 375, 2 from 730, one row from 1260. A panel that would stick out on the right opens leftwards. The choice lives in the address, so a filtered catalog can be shared.

items.title: Grid
items.html: One column below M, two at M, and from L six tracks: the first four cards take half a row, the rest a third — the rhythm of the Figma catalog, kept only in the default order.

items.title: Tabs
items.html: «Все» and «Кофе» show the coffee; каскара, дрипы, сеты and мерч say they are coming (not in the shop yet).

blocks.title: The catalog at 25 screens
blocks.sub: First row: cards in the first row (the first four take half a row from M). Filters: rows of filter cells. First card: its top on the screen.

sections.title: The whole responsive picture
sections.sub: Every role and block size as the browser resolves it, every 10px of width (a screen 1100 tall) and every 25px of height (1440 wide). Dashed grey: round 4 (main). Moved this round: the hero title from L (Round 5 tab: 62 → 90px, flat from about 1500), and with it the hero's cells, rows and the photo above them (Hero tab); the hero's lines now end at the screen's edge below 1520; the info icon (--fact-icon, new: 40 → 56); the plus from its corner; the business gap (= --section-y); the taste cell's side; the newsletter's field beside its line from M (Footer); the recommended row's width past the column is unchanged. The type roles and the spacing roles did not move.

sections.title: Responsive map
sections.sub: What each block does at each width, from the sweep. Accent lines: the shared column steps (S, M, L land at these screen widths because the column is the screen less two gutters). Dashed: the navbar's page step.

items: Round 5 moved no step. The newsletter's line and field go into two halves at M (the shared step); the hero title follows the column from L (a container unit, flat from about 1500); the hairlines that run out to the screen's edges stop at the frame at max. The navbar's sections are one row at its widest step.

Round 3 moved no step. The footer's two halves still start at L; they are squares from about 1360 wide (a content width, not a step: below it the links need more height). The recommended row now runs past the column at every width. The info modal turns into a sheet under 40em (the tab bar's page step).

Round 2 moved the navbar's steps (before: the burger under 64em) and added two: 48em and 40em. The page steps now sit at the screens of the column steps (768 ≈ M, 1024 ≈ L), so with a 16px text the navbar changes together with the blocks. The new container step max (the column at 1520px, from about 1616) frames the hero. No block step moved.
S (22rem column) lands at about 380: it changes small things inside cards (the filter cells, the buy-bar captions), so it shows no row here.
Every block changes at the same two widths, about 750 and 1000; only the navbar has its own step (64em, so bigger browser text gets the burger sooner).
The catalog filter cells wrap by their own width (they flow), so their rows change at 370, 550, 730 and 1260 with no step.

sections.title: Motion
sections.sub: src/styles/base/motion.css: three curves and four times. Round 5: no pack lag, no hover movement; cards sink away out of the column; the info block grows as one card. With «reduce motion» every time is 0 and the packs stand still, without carry or press.

items.name: out
items.use: arriving and settling: hovers, panels, the toast coming in

items.name: pack follow
items.use: the packs follow their targets (scroll lean, pointer turn) at 9 per second

items.name: fade «ease» (new)
items.use: every gradient: the opacity of a fade along its length (16 stops), as tw-easing-gradients

items.name: card carry
items.use: a rising card's pack catches up with its slot: 1 − e^(−9t), soft-capped at 12% of its height (≤ 40px); the page's scroll and a sliding row no longer lag (round 5)

rows.name: product pack turn (one turn over 5 tiles)
rows.label: as long as the scroll through the stage

rows.name: navbar / tab bar cross to a new ground (--t-move)
pack press in / out (16 per second, to 95%)
info block grows as one card (--t-move)
modal text rides with the title (--t-move)
card sinks away out of the column (--t-out, ease-out)
modal steps to the next block
rows.label: 0.23s out + 0.45s in

rows.name: card → coffee page: name and pack travel (--t-move)

items.title: In fast, out slow
items.html: Hovers come in at 0.2s and leave at 0.45s, so a pointer passing over a list leaves a soft trail (as Flow Medium).

items.title: Two loops
items.html: The hero photo drifts 8% over 40s and back; the footer flame burns in 5s (round 3). Both stop with «reduce motion» (the flame shows its first frame).

items.title: Shared elements (round 3)
items.html: Things that belong together travel instead of appearing: a block becomes its modal (its icon, title and plus move; the ground grows), a card becomes its page (name and pack move). Nothing text-bearing is scaled except the name in the page transition, which the browser grows from one size to the other.

items.title: Still (round 5)
items.html: The page's scroll and a sliding row never move or tilt a pack; only a card rising into place carries its pack, which tilts and settles. Hovers never move anything either: they tint.

items.title: Weight
items.html: Pressed anywhere on its card, a pack gives way (further, smaller) and stays while held.

items.title: Colour crossings (new)
items.html: The bars change colour only when wholly over a section, on the travel curve and time, so a boundary never flickers through them.

sections.title: The grammar
sections.sub: How the site is drawn, in plain words, and which of these rules a script checks.

items.title: Colour
items.html: Ink #2d2f33 on paper, cloud #f6f6f6 for surfaces (cards, tiles, the buy bar), graphite and black for dark blocks, lavender for eyebrows and info icons. Secondary text is ink at 70%; 60% only for large text. Every section names its ground; lines and hover tints follow it: ink 20% / white 30%, ink 6% / white 20%.

items.title: Type
items.html: Mono bold capitals tracked 0.05em for names and headings; Apercu for everything read; Technology digits for the countdown. Labels (eyebrows, controls, prices) differ by case and colour, not size.

items.title: Size
items.html: Every size a line from 320 to 1440 on one ladder; the screen's height counts; nothing grows past 1440, the column stops at 1520.

items.title: Shape
items.html: Sharp rectangles divided by hairlines; only pills and dots are round.

items.title: Layout
items.html: Everything sits in the content column; full-bleed blocks put their content in a column too, so they change at the same steps S, M, L.

items.title: Motion
items.html: Three curves, four times, two loops; things that belong together travel (a block becomes its modal as one card); hovers tint and never move; packs move only when their card rises.

blocks.title: Rules
rows: Sizes only from the scale; screen units only where a decision says
Layout steps only at S, M, L, max (and 64em, 48em, 40em, 32em tall)
No rounded corners except pills and dots
Type levels ≥ ×1.125 apart at both ends
One line colour: borders only var(--line)
The navbar's sections never touch the logo or the tools (audit)
The countdown as wide as its caption (audit)
Every fade eased and whole: one var(--fade-*) per place, over the whole block, no solid band under it (rounds 3, 5)
Hovers never move: no transform in a :hover rule (round 5)
Lines run out to the screen's edges beside the column, or stop at its frame (round 5)
A pointer's focus changes nothing; scripts move focus through focusFrom() (round 5)
A whole card is its link; nothing positioned between the link and .card (round 3)
Things that belong together travel (block → modal, card → page) (round 3)
Waiting cards are data-wait; data-out is the filter's (round 3)
Links only to pages that exist
Fixed bars stand on the tab bar (--tabbar-h)
A hover tints only its own item's ground
Every row that scrolls sideways is position: relative
3D canvas at z-index 5; what shows above packs ≥ 6
Links inside the site through href(ctx, to)
One heading level per section; names in mono, text in Apercu
Cells inside a block share hairlines (margin −1px), never double lines

sections.title: Checks
sections.sub: What was checked, how, and what is kept on purpose.

blocks.title: The rules (run on every build and in CI)

items.title: Colours only from tokens
items.how: no #hex, colour functions or named colours in 18 stylesheets

items.title: Sizes only from the scale
items.how: font sizes are --type-* (or the 16px floor of fields, 12px of the counter); screen units only in 5 rules listed in decisions.json

items.title: Layout steps only at S, M, L
items.how: container queries at 22rem, 43rem, 58rem, 1520px on the column; media only through media.css (--links-full 64em, --links 48em, --phone 40em, --short 32em tall, input, motion)

items.title: Motion only from motion.css
items.how: transitions use var(--t-in/out/move) and var(--ease-out/move/leave); the hero's slow drift is the one loop

items.title: Faces only through tokens
items.how: font-family is var(--sans), var(--mono) or var(--digits)

items.title: The scale holds its own rules
items.how: both ends of 35 roles on the ladder, 9 type pairs ≥ ×1.125, 14 colour pairs

items.title: One line colour
items.how: every border is var(--line), set by the ground to ink-20 or white-30 (7 places); states may use ink

items.title: Every fade eased
items.how: gradients are var(--fade-*) (colors.json fades: one per place, eased, over the whole block, no solid band under it) or solid bands for lines

items.title: Hovers never move
items.how: no :hover rule transforms, translates, scales or rotates anything: a hover tints its own ground

items.what: Headings and names are set in PT Mono Bold, as in Figma (self-hosted, cut to the text face's characters: 13 KB)
items.why: the file came from Tim in round 3; its ParaType Free Font Licence allows embedding on web pages. Rounds 1–2 used JetBrains Mono Bold in its place

items.what: From L the footer is two equal halves, each at least a square: the animated flame centred on the left one by its mass (measured over its animation: 50.5% across, 62.9% down its box), the newsletter and the links on the right. Square from about 1360px wide; narrower, the links need more height than the square has and both halves grow with them (1280: 599 × 626)
items.why: Tim, round 3: «2 square-ratio containers», «the logo should be optically centered». The mass centre lifts the flame by 12% of its height, as the Figma footer's 40px lift of a 320px logo does

items.what: The recommended row runs out to the screen's edges (scripts/slider.js measures the column's margins into --bleed-l/-r), padded back so its cards stand and snap on the column; cards rise into place from below as they come into view
items.why: Tim, round 3: «the wrapper of the cards should not crop them», «the new card should move into place from below and opacity 0». A rising card is transformed and translucent for 0.9s, so for that time it is a stacking context and its pack (faded with it: pouch3d alpha) draws above its name and buy row

items.what: Every new arrival shows a photo; a coffee without its own (photos.bySlug) shows the next of four moodboard photos (site.json featured.photos)
items.why: Tim, round 3: «the right column should contain a photo»; only four coffees have a photo

items.what: Pages cross-fade (cross-document view transitions); a card opening its coffee carries its name and pack to the page's title and big pack. For the capture the packs show their stills. Chrome 126+, Safari 18.2+; elsewhere a page simply opens. public/vt.js, a plain script in <head>, names the parts
items.why: Tim, round 3: «a card on a click should transform into a product page seamlessly». The script has to run before the first frame, which Vite's module bundle does not

items.what: The three info blocks are buttons that grow into one modal (Figma info-blocks-modal): a box of --modal-w in the middle of the dimmed screen, a sheet at the foot of a phone's; it steps to the other blocks; the text of the roast block names the next roast live
items.why: Tim, round 3. The ground grows (an empty box may scale), the icon and title travel at their size, the plus turns into the cross: nothing is stretched. While it is open the page stops scrolling and keeps its scrollbar's room as padding (--sbw), so nothing behind it moves

items.what: The countdown digits are Technology Bold, subset to 0–9 and the colon (1.2 KB)
items.why: the font of the Figma hero; the file came from Tim

items.what: Every 3D pack shows the label of Индонезия Суматра Паллунг
items.why: only that label exists as art; products.json gives every coffee art: sumatra-front/back

items.what: Prices are placeholders by price group and weight (data/prices.json: Classic 250 / 680 / 2600 ₽ for 50 г / 200 г / 1 кг, Citric 290 / 780 / 2900, Special 390 / 1180 / 4400)
items.why: the price table has no prices

items.what: The photos are the Figma moodboard's: several show other roasters' packs (SIP, Cafe Public, Paloma, Stereoscope, MARU) and none is QQ's own; they are renders exported from Figma at 1280–1440 px
items.why: no other pictures yet

items.what: The hero shows a still of the Figma video (13456698-hd_1920_1080_30fps), drifting slowly, 1280 px wide
items.why: the video file is not in the Figma file's exports

items.what: The countdown and the catalog's shipping line assume roasting on weekdays at 10:00 Moscow time
items.why: Figma shows a countdown but no schedule

items.what: The texts of the info blocks' modal for payment and delivery were written for the site (the roasting one is Figma's)
items.why: Figma's modal shows only the roasting block's text

items.what: The bag, the favourites, the ratings and the checkout keep everything in the visitor's browser (localStorage, sessionStorage for the checkout); nothing is sent: the checkout's last step, the business request form, «Добавить» an address and «Выйти» say so in a toast
items.why: there is no shop, accounts or CRM behind the site yet; the pages (round 4) are built so they can be reviewed and used as far as a static site can

items.what: Under 48em the sections open from the burger as a plain list
items.why: the menu is not designed

items.what: «Популярные» (the catalog's default order): coffees with a tag first, then Special, then the newest
items.why: no sales data

items.what: «Кофе с похожим вкусом»: the four coffees nearest in density, acidity, sweetness and ferment, nearer for each shared flavour family of descriptors and for the same line
items.why: the table has no explicit links between coffees

items.what: Secondary text is ink-70 (#2d2f33 at 70%), never ink-60 or ink-50 as some Figma texts are (the unchosen weight «1 кг», small numbers of the pager)
items.why: ink-60 is 3.8 : 1 on white and ink-50 2.9 : 1, below 4.5 : 1 for text; ink-60 stays only for large text (the inactive catalog tabs, 3 : 1) and parts of controls

items.what: No rounded corners: blocks, cards, buttons and fields are sharp; only pills (descriptors, the bag counter) and dots are round
items.why: the brand's grid of hairlines; Figma has no radius except pills

items.what: The navbar is 48px at every size, its links in --type-body; its own side margin is 16px (the small gutter) and its content stops at the column widened by the 8px of air inside the logo's and icons' boxes
items.why: a control, not a block: as in every Figma frame; Tim, round 2: the side padding «small», a systematic max width counting the air around the logo and the icons

items.what: The hero is the screen less a 24px peek (less the tab bar on a phone), at most --hero-max (960 → 1200); never less than its cells, the fade and --hero-photo need
items.why: a screen-sized block (the rule of the system: such blocks are measured by the screen's height directly); Tim, round 2: «full minus 24px» with a min and a max by screen size

items.what: From L the hero's title fills its cell: its longest word «обжарки» (4.55em) runs from the cell's edge to its padding, so its size is a third of the column less the padding, ÷ 4.55, never less than --type-display and never more than its size at the column's 1520px (so it never shrinks as the frame comes in): 62px at 1024, 88px at 1440, 90px from about 1500 (it was 64px at most). From about 1366 its three lines and their padding set the height of the cells and the countdown's and the links' three rows share it; on narrower L screens the countdown's digits are taller and lead
items.why: Tim, round 5: «the title should shape the height of the whole bottom container; on larger screens its size should be larger than now». The size follows the cell, which only a container unit (cqi of the column) knows; the type scale stops at 1440

items.what: The product stage is pinned at the height of the screen less the navbar and the buy bar; the fact tiles are spaced by 40% of the screen's height (28% from L)
items.why: the pack turns as the tiles pass: the distance between them is scroll time, which is measured in screens

items.what: Everything in the roast cell is as wide as its caption «До ближайшей обжарки» (13.9em of --type-control): the digits are --type-control × 13.9 / 3, the date (more than a day to wait) × 13.9 / (0.65 × its letters) in mono
items.why: Tim, round 2: «the elements should be the max width of the caption»; Technology has no Cyrillic, so the date «Пт, 9 Окт» is set in the mono of the headings

items.what: Four coffees show a photo on their card instead of the 3D pack (data/site.json photos), as the Figma catalog mixes them
items.why: the rhythm of the Figma catalog

items.what: On a narrow column the buy bar stays at the foot of the screen in two rows (options; quantity, price, button)
items.why: Figma has the bar only at 1440; buying should stay one tap away

items.what: On a screen under 32em tall (a phone sideways) the buy bar waits after the product stage instead of following the screen, and the stage pins at the whole screen under the navbar (no 22rem floor)
items.why: measured at 844 × 390: the two-row bar took 129 of 390px and covered the pack by 139px; a pinned block must fit the screen or not pin

items.what: The navbar in four steps: every section (≥ 64em), four short ones «Каталог, Бизнесу, Журнал, Контакты» (≥ 48em), the burger, and under 40em a tab bar at the foot of the screen with «Каталог, Корзина, Избранное, Профиль»
items.why: Tim, round 2; the widths are the screens of the column steps L and M (1024, 768), where each row fits with room to spare (measured)

items.what: Navbar and tab-bar items link only to pages that exist: the catalog, «Кофейням» / «Бизнесу» (business/), «Контакты», favourites, bag and profile do; «Каскара», «Дрипы», «Сеты», «Офисам», «Журнал» and search are labels without a link
items.why: Tim, round 2: «links to pages, not anchors; if there's no page, don't add any link»

items.what: The navbar (and the tab bar) take the colours of the section under them, changing once wholly over it, on --t-move; above the top of the page they keep the first section's
items.why: Tim, round 2

items.what: Hover on a control (the navbar's links and icons, the tab bar, the hero's links and «i», the pager's numbers, the arrows, a card's two cells and its heart): a tint behind the one item, white at 20% on dark grounds, ink at 6% on light ones (white would not show on white); nothing moves. A pointer's focus changes nothing; the keyboard's draws the ring
items.why: Tim, round 2: «semi-transparent white, not affecting other elements»; round 5: «these elements on hover should change the color of the container to semi-transparent cool gray or white… in the focused state nothing should be changed», «the icon shouldn't move», «the picture should not move on hover»
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 (rounds 2 and 5); Claude (the light-ground tint, the keyboard's ring kept)

items.what: Every hairline is var(--line): cool grey at 20% on light grounds, white at 30% on dark ones; only states (the current dot of the pager, a field focused from the keyboard) draw a border in ink
items.why: Tim, round 2: «borders always cool gray 20% on light and white 30% on dark»

items.what: The account pages show a made-up visitor, «Марк Новиков» of Figma, with six orders (data/account.json); every number on them (lots, processes, Q, countries, descriptors, the taste profile, beans, totals) is worked out from those orders and the catalog by src/templates/account-data.mjs
items.why: there are no accounts yet; Figma's numbers did not add up (an order of three coffees at 680 ₽ for 1095 ₽), so the pages compute them

items.what: Delivery prices and the free-delivery threshold: courier 415 ₽, pickup 240 ₽, 1–2 days, free from 1 799 ₽ (data/site.json shop)
items.why: Figma shows 415 ₽ in the bag and 490 ₽ in the checkout for the same courier; one value everywhere

items.what: Of the 15 questions of «Вопросы и ответы» Figma answers one («Как выбрать кофе?»); the other 14 answers are written from what the site already says (delivery, payment, the roast) and marked placeholder in data/faq.json
items.why: the page needs answers to work

items.what: The business page keeps the copywriter's blanks of Figma visible: [чемпионат, год], [название], [N] лотов, [N] минут
items.why: inventing them would put false claims on the site

items.what: The privacy policy keeps the blanks of its Figma text: ОГРНИП [указать], ИНН [указать], адрес [указать]; it names qqcoffee@mail.ru while the contacts name sales@qqcoffee.ru
items.why: legal details must come from the company, not be guessed

items.what: The team portraits of «О компании» are the Figma stock photos (Pexels); Figma repeats seven people twice, the site shows each once. The Instagram strip has no link (Figma gives no account address)
items.why: no team photos yet

items.what: The two maps of the contacts are pictures from Figma (both crops of one map screenshot, not of the real addresses); each links to its address on Yandex Maps
items.why: an embedded map would need a third-party script and a CSP exception

items.what: Pages drawn with older colours or styles in Figma follow the system instead: the bag's cards are the cloud squares of the catalog's half cards (Figma: a warm photo ground and hairlines #c0c1c2 at 30%), the orange roast line of the bag is ink-70, the purple «Заявка» button of the business page is white on ink, the green «Доставлен» is ink (lavender stays the state of an order on its way), radii of 4px are sharp
items.why: Tim, round 4: «some pages use older colours or other things — be systematic»
items.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 (the rule, round 4: «be systematic»); Claude (each case)

Measured on the home page: black over the hero, white over the coffees, black over «Наш подход», white over «О компании», cool grey over business, white over the facts. The tab bar follows the section at the screen's foot the same way.

items.ask: 9. Smaller sizes: short links, then the burger, then a bottom menu
items.done: Four steps: every section from 64em (1024), «Каталог, Бизнесу, Журнал, Контакты» from 48em (768), the burger below, and under 40em (640) the favourites, bag and profile leave for a tab bar at the foot with «Каталог, Корзина, Избранное, Профиль». The widths are the screens of the column steps L and M, where each row fits with room to spare (the sections 584px + two outer columns of 172px at 1024; the short ones 288 + 2 × 172 at 768). The audit now fails if the sections touch the logo or the tools.

items.ask: 10. Links to pages, not anchors; no page, no link
items.done: Only «Кофе» and «Каталог» link (to the catalog). Каскара, Дрипы, Сеты, Кофейням, Офисам, Бизнесу, Журнал, Контакты, search, favourites, bag and profile are labels without a link (<a> without href) until their page exists; each becomes a link by adding its path in data/site.json (decision nav-links-pages). The hero's and the footer's links are unchanged: should the same rule apply there?

items.ask: 11. Scrolling above the page turns it white
items.done: Above the top (a touchpad or phone bounce) the bars keep the first section's ground (black on the home page), and the page behind the bounce is that colour too: the top half of the page bounces in its first ground, the bottom half in its last (the footer's cloud). A real bounce cannot be made in a headless browser: please check on your Mac and phone.

items.ask: 12. A counter only on the bag
items.done: The favourites count is gone (navbar and tab bar); the bag keeps its lavender count.

items.ask: 1. Height: full minus 24px; a system of min and max
items.done: The screen less 24 (less the 56px tab bar on a phone), at most --hero-max (960 → 1200: a portrait tablet, a 2560 screen), and never less than the cells, the fade (--hero-fade 64 → 160) and a strip of photo (--hero-photo 48 → 120) need. Measured: 876 at 1440 × 900 (was 800), 1056 at 1920 × 1080, 744 at 1024 × 768, 764 at 390 × 844; 1067 at 820 × 1180 and 1200 at 2560 × 1440 (the max). Short phones get the content's height: 638 at 320 × 568.

items.ask: 2. Ease the black gradient
items.done: An eased fade in 16 stops along an S-curve (cubic-bezier 0.42, 0, 0.58, 1), as tw-easing-gradients, generated into --fade-black from colors.json; 160px tall at 1440 (was 48px, two stops). The featured photo caption and the business cards use the same fade.

items.ask: 3. All texts in the three blocks trimmed
items.done: text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic on the title, the day row, the digits, the caption and the links: each row's padding is the space you see (12 → 20px). Chrome and Safari 18.2+; Firefox keeps the line's air.

items.ask: 4. Title always three lines
items.done: Word under word, at every width: 3 lines at all 25 screens measured (before 1 or 2 lines below 1024).

items.ask: 5. The middle block in three containers, aligned with the three links
items.done: From M the countdown and the links share three equal rows (CSS subgrid): the day and the time beside «Каталог», the digits beside «Бизнесу», the caption beside «Контакты». Centres within 0px at every screen measured (before 3–13px off). Rows are as tall as the digits need: 104px at 1440.

items.ask: 6. Left and right border on the inner container from a max width
items.done: A new container step max (1520px: the column at its most). From there the cells are framed by a hairline on each side and the title stands 48px off the left one. 1440 has none; 1680, 1920 and 2560 have them.

items.ask: 7. Hover on the links
items.done: The link's whole cell gets the hover tint (white 20%), and the arrow keeps its 6px nudge.

items.ask: 8. Elements as wide as «ДО БЛИЖАЙШЕЙ ОБЖАРКИ»
items.done: The caption is 13.9em of the control size; the day row is that wide, the digits are sized to it (control × 13.9 / 3), and the countdown font is now tabular (every digit as wide as «0»), so it is exactly as wide every second: 275 = 275 at 1440, 200 = 200 at 390. The audit checks it at every size (decision countdown-as-caption).

items.ask: 9. More than 24h to wait: the date and «До ближайшей обжарки»
items.done: From Friday 10:00 to Sunday 10:00 (with the placeholder weekday schedule) the digits give way to the date of the next roast, «ПН, 26 ОКТ», in the mono of the headings (Technology has no Cyrillic), sized by its letters to the caption's width; screen readers hear «Следующая обжарка в понедельник, 26 октября».

items.ask: 10. On load the bar rises in from opacity 0 and from below
items.done: The cells rise one section gap (24 → 48px) and fade in over 0.9s on --ease-out, 0.2s after the page opens (--t-rise, new). Not with «reduce motion».

items.ask: Always cool gray 20% on light and white 30% on dark
items.done: One --line, set by each section's ground: ink 20% on white and cloud, white 30% on black and cool grey. Changed: the navbar's line (ink 10% → 20%), the hero's (white 40% → 30%), the featured pack square and the product lots (ink 10%), arrows, fields and the catalog panel (#d5d5d6 or ink). A new rule in build/rules.mjs fails any border that is not var(--line); only states (the current pager dot, a focused field) may draw in ink, and drawn marks (the weight dot, a chevron) in currentColor.

blocks.title: What this changes that you may not expect
items: The hero is taller than the screen on small and sideways phones: 638 at 320 × 568 (it was 555), 549 at 844 × 390 (was 376) — three title lines and a countdown as wide as its caption take more room. From 390 × 844 up it is the screen less 24.
Most navbar items lead nowhere now (no page behind them): only «Кофе» / «Каталог» are links. On a phone, «Корзина», «Избранное», «Профиль» in the tab bar do nothing yet.
At 1024–1600 the navbar's logo no longer lines up with the content column (it stands at 16px; the column at the gutter, up to 48px): that is the «small» padding. From 1616 on they line up.
The navbar on light grounds hovers in ink, not white (white would be invisible on white).
On a phone the page ends 56px lower (the tab bar's room under the footer), and the product's pinned stage is 56px shorter.
The countdown is a little smaller than before at 1440 (93 instead of 96px): its size now follows the caption.

items.ask: Start with the main, catalog and product pages; other pages only as context

items.ask: Figma is general inspiration, not exact values or structure
items.done: Sizes come from the site's own scale; structure follows Figma (sections, cells, hairlines, mono capitals). Where Figma differs between frames, the site takes one line through them: e.g. h2 32→48 where Figma has 32 / 36 / 40 / 48 steps.

items.ask: A fluid system, not breakpoints (exceptions allowed)
items.done: Every size is a straight line from its value at 320 to its value at 1440 (31 roles in design/scale.json), constant outside; the screen's height counts (a screen 360 tall gets the 320 sizes, 920 tall the 1440 sizes). Layout changes at only three shared column steps S 22rem, M 43rem, L 58rem, plus the navbar at 64em. Four exceptions use screen units on purpose, listed in decisions.json.

items.ask: A system within pages and between screen sizes
items.done: One ladder (steps 2/4/8/16), type levels ≥ ×1.125 apart at both ends, colours only from design/colors.json with contrast checks, one motion vocabulary; build/rules.mjs checks 9 rules on every build and in CI.

items.ask: Flow Medium's size system as inspiration

blocks.title: Where the site departs from Figma, or does something you may not expect
items: Headings are JetBrains Mono, not PT Mono: narrower, with a different «Ж» and «Ш». A licence for PT Mono Bold swaps it in one line.
Sizes in between Figma frames are not Figma's: the site draws one line through each role, so e.g. the hero title is 55 at 1024 where Figma would show 56 (768 frame) or 64 (990 frame).
The countdown is 96 at 1440 and above, where Figma's 1920 frame has 128: nothing grows past 1440.
Figma's featured slide has a photo; the site shows the 3D pack unless data/site.json names a photo for that coffee.
On a phone sideways the hero is taller than the screen (555 px at 568 × 320): the title, the countdown and three links stack in one column below M.
The photos are Figma's moodboard, several with other roasters' packs: to replace before launch.
